picks.title: Digital Books: HathiTrust Awarded $5 Million, 5-Year Mellon Grant to Enable AI-Driven Access and Discovery
picks.excerpt: HathiTrust, with Northeastern University Library and Authors Alliance, won a five-year, $5M Mellon Foundation grant for “Transparent Books: AI Infrastructure for Discovery and the Public Interest,” applying AI to improve descriptive metadata and text quality across 19 million digitized volumes and to supply verified, traceable book text and images for academic and noncommercial use.
picks.rationale: The consented counter-model to Amazon's shredding warehouse and Anthropic's Project Panama — 19 million volumes turned into a traceable, permissioned corpus, which changes where researchers and publishers can legitimately source book text.

picks.title: Production Companies, Literary Agents, Foreign Languages: AI-Driven Scams Continue to Morph
picks.excerpt: Writer Beware documents how author-targeting scams have been rebuilt on generative AI — fake production companies, impersonated literary agents, and newly fluent foreign-language solicitations that no longer betray themselves through broken English.
picks.rationale: Most actionable item in the pool: generative AI has erased the broken-English tell that authors and freelancers used to screen predatory approaches, so the vetting checklist has to be rebuilt from scratch.

picks.title: AI가 소설 쓰는 시대, 작품 고르는 일이 더 어려워졌다: 일본 문학상이 직면한 새로운 과제
picks.excerpt: 니혼게이자이신문 보도를 인용해, AI로 쓴 소설이 일본 문학상 공모에 몰리면서 심사 부담이 급증했다고 전한다. 제14회 하야카와 SF 콘테스트 응모작은 예년 400편 안팎에서 1012편으로 두 배 이상 늘었고, 제13회 호시 신이치상 일반부문 수상작 4편 중 3편이 창작 과정에 AI를 활용했다.
picks.rationale: Hard numbers on a judging system buckling under AI submissions — Hayakawa SF entries jumping from ~400 to 1,012, and three of four Hoshi Shinichi winners using AI — a submission-and-selection shift no other candidate covers.

picks.title: Vietnam's Publishing Sector Has New Rules and Wants AI Content Labelled
picks.excerpt: Vietnam's revised publishing law introduces mandatory labelling for AI-generated content alongside tightened copyright provisions for the book trade. It joins the EU AI Act and China's draft standards in making AI disclosure a legal requirement rather than a publisher choice.
picks.rationale: A third jurisdiction turning AI disclosure from a publisher policy into statute — the labelling obligation is now a distribution requirement any author selling into these markets has to plan for.

picks.title: The Heart of the Matter: Copyright, AI Training, and LLMs – Part 3: Fair Use and AI Training Under US Law
picks.excerpt: CCC walks through how the recent federal court decisions actually apply the US fair use defense to AI model training — which acquisition and copying steps courts have blessed, which they have not, and what that leaves rightsholders able to license.
picks.rationale: Written by the collective licensing body rather than a reporter: it converts the fair-use rulings into the practical question authors and publishers keep asking — which rights are still yours to sell for AI training.
